title: Producers and consumer groups
dek: A producer's guarantees stop at sessions and retries, and a consumer's position says what was handed over, not what was finished. This fourth part of a five-part teardown reads the clients of Apache Kafka 4.4.0: two threads around a queue, what linger really decides, a key hash that differs by client, the broker state idempotence leans on and the places it runs out, a commit decoded byte by byte, the classic barrier against KIP-848's heartbeat, and share groups that replace ownership with leases.
byline: 6 November 2026 · Subject: kafka@1156b275 (Apache Kafka 4.4.0) · Part 4 of 5 · Read from the source; measured where this machine allows
description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 4: the producer's accumulator and Sender, linger and batch size, partitioners across clients, idempotence and where it runs out, consumer position and commits, classic and KIP-848 rebalances, static membership and share groups.
og_description: Part 4 of a five-part Kafka teardown at 1156b275 (4.4.0): two threads around a queue, linger against batch.size, broker dedupe state and where it runs out, the first-batch overtake (KAFKA-19880), a commit decoded by hand, the classic barrier against KIP-848, and share-group leases. Timings are loopback on a shared 2-vCPU box: relative only.
